thread:
oliver: quick question for the group  do we keep red asterisks for required fields or switch to the visible 'Required' pill? a11y and localization are the main concerns.
tess: my vote is visible 'Required' text. screen readers announce it better and translators can handle it explicitly.
mina: agree on clarity, but can we make it low-contrast so it doesn't compete with the label? e.g., #6b6b6b instead of bright red.
oliver: good call. the contrast needs to still meet legible thresholds though. aria-bot: (scan) 5 fields fail contrast when using muted gray.
aria-bot: accessibility check: required-label-contrast-fail for 5 inputs. recommend 3:1 contrast for non-critical auxiliary text.
tess: ok, so slightly darker gray then. also: prefer 'Required' after the label vs prefix? thoughts?
mina: after label reads more naturally in LTR languages. prefix can be odd. Keep after.
devops-bot: FYI, implementing visible 'Required' will add ~120 chars in the DOM and slightly more CSS, negligible perf.
oliver: thanks. next: inline validation strategy. should validation run on blur, on submit, or on every keystroke?
tess: blur for most fields. passwords and email can validate earlier. keystroke validation is noisy for assistive tech.
mina: agree. also for long forms we should add a top summary on submit listing all errors with anchor links to fields. anchors should focus fields without moving viewport abruptly.
oliver: implement anchor focusing like: ```js
const target = document.getElementById('field-123');
target.focus({preventScroll: true});
target.scrollIntoView({behavior: prefersReducedMotion ? 'auto' : 'smooth', block: 'center'});
```
devops-bot: note: smooth scrolling may be disabled by browser settings; respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
tess: great. UX nit: when we focus an invalid field, we should also expose the inline error text by default (not hidden behind a hover).
mina: accessibility nit: make sure the inline error is in the DOM and has role="alert" for AT to announce changes. only announce on submit/blur to avoid repetitive noise.
oliver: deleting resources: modal typed-confirm vs undo toast. which to use for deleting workspaces?
tess: workspace deletion is severe. typed-confirm (enter workspace name) + a server-side grace window (soft-delete for 7 days) seems safe.
mina: power users might complain. offer org-level setting to relax to toast undo for orgs that opt-in. default should be conservative.
devops-bot: also add audit log entry and require an admin permission check for delete.
aria-bot: accessibility checklist: modal must trap focus, use aria-modal, focus the text input on open, and announce the danger level.
oliver: copy suggestion: header: "Permanently delete workspace" body: "Type the workspace name to confirm. This will permanently remove all data and cannot be undone within the retention window." primary CTA: "Delete workspace" (red).
tess: one more thing  password fields: avoid live erroring that reveals password rules as they type. show rules but only surface 'meets requirements' after submit or on explicit show.
mina: agreed. i'll draft compact + expanded specs (visual tokens, copy, a11y annotations) and share a figma file.
oliver: perfect. i'll queue the dev tickets and we'll pair on the modal implementation next week. thanks! :white_check_mark:
